prospects.thesis: Lockheed is the premier prime contractor with unmatched exposure to F-35 production, missile defense (PAC-3, THAAD), and hypersonics — all priority buckets in the FY27 defense budget. Bullish options flow combined with bullish institutional positioning and a reasonable 1.7x P/S suggests smart money is positioning ahead of continued foreign military sales momentum and replenishment orders tied to ongoing geopolitical tensions. The +7.7% 1M move shows momentum without being overextended.

Booz Allen is the leading defense/intelligence IT consultant, well-positioned as the Pentagon accelerates AI, cyber, and digital modernization spending — a structurally growing sub-niche distinct from hardware primes. Bullish options flow despite bearish institutional read suggests a potential contrarian setup, and the +16.6% 1M rip indicates the tape is already recognizing the catalyst. P/S of 0.9x remains reasonable for a services compounder.

HII is the sole builder of U.S. nuclear-powered aircraft carriers and a key submarine producer (Virginia/Columbia class) — a shipbuilding sub-niche with a multi-decade backlog and bipartisan Navy funding tailwinds. Bullish institutional flow and +10.3% 1M momentum reflect accelerating recognition of AUKUS-related submarine demand and Navy shipbuilding plan upgrades. At 0.9x P/S, valuation leaves room for multiple expansion.

Northrop owns the B-21 Raider stealth bomber program and Sentinel ICBM modernization — the two most strategically critical nuclear-triad programs, a distinct sub-niche from Lockheed's fighter/missile focus. Bullish institutional positioning plus +8.3% 1M momentum suggest the market is beginning to price in B-21 production ramp catalysts into 2027. Reasonable 1.8x P/S for a sole-source monopolist on key programs.

PATH provides theme diversification as the only AI/ML name on the screen, representing the agentic AI/RPA pure-play as enterprises operationalize generative AI into workflow automation. Bullish institutional signal with a -5.5% 1M pullback creates an attractive risk/reward entry ahead of potential enterprise AI budget flush in Q4. However, elevated VIX (25.74) and risk-off tape warrant waiting for confirmation before committing.

market_pulse.rotation_analysis: Big money is piling into Real Estate in a way that's hard to ignore — the options market is betting aggressively that REITs are about to catch a bid, which usually happens when traders sniff out rate cuts coming sooner than the Fed is signaling, and with housing affordability now a bipartisan talking point heading into budget fights, there's real chatter about targeted housing credits and relaxed lending rules that would juice the sector. Industrials getting quiet bullish flow fits the infrastructure-and-reshoring narrative too — every tariff headline and CHIPS-style spending bill funnels money into domestic builders and machinery names. On the flip side, the heavy bearish positioning in Financials, Consumer Discretionary, and Staples tells me the smart money is bracing for the consumer to crack — credit spreads widening and junk bonds (HYG) getting hammered in options confirms people are quietly buying insurance against a credit event, even while stocks look calm on the surface. Healthcare getting dumped is likely political: drug pricing executive orders, Medicare negotiation expansions, and election-year posturing make the sector a punching bag, and Energy's bearish flow lines up with the administration pushing to keep gasoline prices low plus softer China demand.
